why:
RE-VERDICTED 2026-09-03 (phase-379 W6 decision 1), rename -> divergence: the name MATCHED (`Subscription<M>::take(M&)`, renamed from `try_recv`), and what the report called a difference was the second parameter. rclcpp's is `take(ROSMessageType&, MessageInfo&)`; ours takes the message only, because there is no per-sample message-info channel to fill it from -- most backends carry none, and the one that does (zenoh, via the wire attachment) exposes it separately as `take_serialized_with_attachment`. Adding an out-parameter that three of four backends would leave zeroed is the shape RFC-0036 exists to refuse. See `c:take` for the verb decision and `cpp:MessageInfo` for the type.

AMENDED 2026-09-18 (phase-456 W2b): the name no longer matches, because ours moved to `nros::PollSubscription<M>::take`. WHY, and it is not the reason the phase doc gave: upstream DOES have `rclcpp::Subscription::take` (two overloads, `subscription.hpp`) -- what upstream does not have is a subscriber the CALLER owns. Its `take` is called on a node-owned entity after a `WaitSet` reports it ready. We have no wait set, so the entity that can answer a take is the caller-owned one, and the entity that carries the upstream NAME is the dispatch one a ported file declares as `Subscription<M>::SharedPtr`. Those are two different objects here and one object upstream; the name went to the dispatch half and the verb went with the storage. The alternative -- keeping `take()` on the dispatch class -- is what shipped until W2b, and it compiled into an unfilled `RmwSubscriber` rather than refusing.
